January 28, 2025

![An illustration of a squirrel holding an acorn, a person with pigtails holding an open laptop, a robot holding a flower, and a person writing in a notebook](data:image/png;base64,)![An illustration of a squirrel holding an acorn, a person with pigtails holding an open laptop, a robot holding a flower, and a person writing in a notebook](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/db2943188f0ced58b2f840bc09b3acce85c331c9-760x428.png?w=1632&h=919&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

In a time of blurred roles, new technology, and breakneck product cycles, how do we uphold craft and purpose in our work?

Hero illustration by Zoey Kim

We asked [six members of the Figma team](https://www.figma.com/blog/six-memos/)

working across design, development, and community to offer up their vision for how we might approach building software in 2025. We hope these memos will help validate and challenge your team as you chart a course for the new year.

[![A squirrel holds an envelope in its paws](data:image/png;base64,)![A squirrel holds an envelope in its paws](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/00a08d5ed712ab537090f92b8b7311f3fb22ec3b-2160x1216.png?w=2160&h=1216&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)](https://www.figma.com/blog/newsletter/)

## [Personalize the web](#personalize-the-web)

As more people and businesses go online, the demand for an internet that caters to a broad set of needs has grown. Product Designer Chia Amisola wonders what we may have overlooked in the process—and how we might get back to building sites that feel more personal and poetic.

[![An illustration of a person typing at a computer with a red flower on the screen, superimposed with frames depicting gnomes watering and arranging other flowers.](data:image/png;base64,)![An illustration of a person typing at a computer with a red flower on the screen, superimposed with frames depicting gnomes watering and arranging other flowers.](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/037649cb0f052d4f2997242a8300d71aa4be3b37-1260x730.png?w=528&h=306&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)](https://www.figma.com/blog/making-space-for-a-handmade-web/)

[**Read more**](https://www.figma.com/blog/making-space-for-a-handmade-web/)

## [Build a competitive moat](#build-a-competitive-moat)

Our relationship to technology changes over time. For Head of Insights Andrew Hogan, becoming a father to two kids has revealed why emotional resonance—not just features—makes software truly distinct and meaningful. He makes the case for why building for an emotional response can give apps a competitive edge.

[![An illustration of two squirrels inspecting an acorn under a magnifying glass](data:image/png;base64,)![An illustration of two squirrels inspecting an acorn under a magnifying glass](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/4dba34211f09be0d753b35074c16ea6b00a7114f-1260x730.png?w=528&h=306&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)](https://www.figma.com/blog/the-new-competitive-moat-is-emotion/)

[**Read more**](https://www.figma.com/blog/the-new-competitive-moat-is-emotion/)

## [Off-road the roadmap](#off-road-the-roadmap)

Launching new products isn’t just about sticking to a singular vision, says Director of Product Avantika Gomes. In fact, great products are defined as much by unexpected twists and turns in the journey as they are by a carefully plotted roadmap. She outlines the risk of holding too tightly to specific solutions, and shares how to make room to pivot.

[![An illustration of an octopus in a pink cap writing in a notepad and holding various objects in its other arms.](data:image/png;base64,)![An illustration of an octopus in a pink cap writing in a notepad and holding various objects in its other arms.](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/0485eca9c6919de2e5a94484737afef2da042d2e-1260x730.png?w=528&h=306&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)](https://www.figma.com/blog/when-to-off-road-the-product-roadmap/)

[**Read more**](https://www.figma.com/blog/when-to-off-road-the-product-roadmap/)

## [Rabbit hole](#rabbit-hole)

![1) UX of a color gradient plugin, 2) a structure made of spheres and rods, 3) an illustration of various shapes connected by a double-ended arrow](data:image/png;base64,)![1) UX of a color gradient plugin, 2) a structure made of spheres and rods, 3) an illustration of various shapes connected by a double-ended arrow](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/303cf4af5e9a2fa734f1d0db42fa23624e967e12-1300x730.png?rect=0,1,1300,729&w=804&h=451&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

1.  Developer Jake Albaugh urges us to [tap into the web’s true expressive potential](https://www.figma.com/blog/why-developers-should-embrace-creative-coding-again/) à la the work of creative coder [Henry Desroches](https://henry.codes/).
2.  Double clicking on [the generalist conversation](https://every.to/chain-of-thought/why-generalists-own-the-future), Content Strategist Carly Ayres offers why [it’s never been more valuable to be in a hybrid role](https://www.figma.com/blog/the-rise-of-the-generalist/).
3.  In making [the case for inclusivity](https://www.figma.com/blog/its-time-we-expand-our-definition-of-design/) and belonging at work, Advocate Kaitie Chambers recommends [_The Art of Gathering_ by Priya Parker](https://www.priyaparker.com/book-art-of-gathering).
